newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bullion house sees gold in $380-$385 range.
newsitem.headline: Japan bullion house sees gold in $380-$385 range.

text.p: Japan's leading bullion house, Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo K.K, said on Tuesday that it expects gold prices to move within a range of between $380 and $385 per ounce for the rest of 1996, unless U.S. shares slump.
The bullion house said gold has been on a upward trend over a long-term period, backed by a global supply shortage. It said $380 was likely to provide support for the rest of 1996.

"Gold prices are unlikely to stray from the ranges for the rest of the year. But I would not rule out the possibility that gold could rise if U.S. stock prices fall sharply," said Makoto Tonoki, general manager of Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo's precious metals division.

He told a gold seminar in Tokyo that gold could rise if President Bill Clinton wins the U.S. presidential election in November and then raises U.S. interest rates -- something that would push down the U.S. stock market.

"If the Dow industrial average falls to the 5,000-level in reaction to the expected hike in U.S. interest rates after the election, gold prices could rise by at least $10 from the current levels," Tonoki said.
Bullion was quoted at $381.10/50 per ounce at 0850 GMT.

Tanaka Kikinzoku said the average gold price in the first nine months of this year was $391.60, against last year's average of $384.16. Tonoki said news that Belgium had finished selling gold reserves was unlikely to have a significant impact on the bullion market. He said Belgian gold sales had been small compared with total gold reserves held by governments.
Belgian National Bank governor Alfons Verplaetse said on Monday there would be no more gold sales by the central bank, after sales of about 700 tonnes in recent years.
